attachments.insertion_landmark: lateral sclera, ~7mm posterior to the corneal limbus (longest tendon of the 4 recti)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: True insertion is onto the sclera of the eyeball, not a fixed bony point; the eyeball is not modeled as its own rigid body with rotational DOF in this pass (a natural candidate for a small future extension), so this muscle's insertion is given relative to the orbital bone frame as an engineering approximation of its resting position rather than a moving attachment.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_to: muscle origin at the common tendinous ring
motor_endplate_zones.notes: The abducens nerve divides into superior and inferior intramuscular branches ~37mm posterior to the insertion; both branches' terminal arborizations end, on average, at 52.9% (SD 3.5%) of total muscle length from the insertion -- the range given is that mean +/- 1 SD. In 84% of specimens the superior and inferior branch territories did not overlap, i.e. LR has two largely separate neuromuscular subterritories rather than one homogeneous zone.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Nam YS, Kim IB, Shin SY, 'Detailed anatomy of the abducens nerve in the lateral rectus muscle', Clin Anat 30(7):873-877 (2017), doi:10.1002/ca.22918 (https://doi.org/10.1002/ca.22918) -- 32 LR specimens, Sihler staining -- retrieved via PubMed

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: EMG-guided percutaneous injection (Alan Scott technique): after topical anesthetic (e.g. proparacaine) and a topical vasoconstrictor, a fine EMG needle is inserted percutaneously (or trans-conjunctivally over the lateral globe) and advanced into the LR belly, most often aiming for its posterior two-thirds; the awake patient is asked to make voluntary gaze shifts into abduction (LR's field of action) while EMG is recorded at the needle tip to confirm intramuscular placement before injecting.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Sub-Tenon/intramuscular, injected preferentially in the posterior two-thirds to middle of the belly rather than right at the insertion.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: EMG burst discharge time-locked to attempted abduction confirms the needle tip is within LR rather than in orbital fat or an adjacent muscle.
structures_at_risk: globe (perforation, the main reported risk of EMG-guided EOM injection generally, though none occurred in the largest published series)
abducens nerve trunk, which divides into two branches ~37mm posterior to the insertion -- injecting too far posteriorly risks blocking the nerve rather than the muscle
lacrimal gland and vessels, lying superotemporal to LR
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: The most extensively documented EMG-guided EOM injection technique in the literature, used for esotropia (weakening an overacting LR) or, as the antagonist injection, alongside medial rectus bupivacaine to correct exotropia. Guidance is by needle-tip EMG, never ultrasound.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Debert I, Miller JM, Danh KK, Scott AB, 'Pharmacologic injection treatment of comitant strabismus', J AAPOS 20(2):106-111.e2 (2016), doi:10.1016/j.jaapos.2015.11.011 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jaapos.2015.11.011) -- 55 adults, EMG-guided technique, PMC4833878 -- retrieved via PubMed
